title: Recycling right, not wishcycling
description: Putting the wrong things in the recycling bin can spoil the whole batch — here is how to get it right.

body.heading: What wishcycling is
paragraphs: Wishcycling is tossing something into recycling because you hope it can be recycled — greasy pizza boxes, coffee cups, plastic bags. Contamination can make whole loads harder or impossible to process.
Local rules differ, so the golden rule is: check your local list. Most councils and cities publish a simple guide of what goes in which bin.

body.heading: Clean, dry, and loose
paragraphs: In most places, recycling should be clean, dry, and loose — rinse food from containers, let them dry, and do not bag recyclables unless your local rules say to.
Keep lids and labels as your local guide directs; rules vary because processing equipment varies. When in doubt, the local list beats a general guess.

body.heading: The unsure pile
paragraphs: For items you are unsure about — batteries, electronics, textiles — look for dedicated drop-off points. Many shops and recycling centres take them free, keeping hazardous parts out of general waste.

takeaway: Check your local list, keep recycling clean and dry, and use drop-off points for batteries and electronics.
